- **Presenting complaint:** Witnessed sudden-onset syncope (~1 hour prior to evaluation), no prodrome (no lightheadedness, nausea, diaphoresis, palpitations, or visual changes).

The case presents a classic, well-evaluated episode of syncope with rigorous exclusion of life-threatening and alternative etiologies. The sudden onset *without prodrome*, immediate full recovery to baseline (no post-ictal deficit), and absence of cardiac structural/arrhythmic, neurological, metabolic, orthostatic, or hypoxemic causes strongly favor reflex (neurally mediated) syncope. Reflex (neurally mediated) syncope, cardioinhibitory-predominant vasovagal syncope.
